intro: Most of my papers end in a model that can be argued with. These four come up again and again across the research.

frameworks.name: The unit of commerce
frameworks.lede: The unit of advertising is moving from the screen, to the audience, to the decision and, if the industry can prove it, to the outcome. Each step moves value towards whoever understands inventory best.

stages.name: Screen
stages.detail: Sell a location, priced by panel.

stages.name: Audience
stages.detail: Sell reachable people, priced by CPM.

stages.name: Decision
stages.detail: Sell the best choice, made continuously.

frameworks.name: The seven-stage proof chain
frameworks.lede: The old chain stopped at brand lift. Buyers now ask whether anyone noticed, whether the ad caused the change, and whether the evidence can steer a live campaign.
frameworks.sourceLabel: From Brand Lift to Incremental Impact

frameworks.name: Five kinds of outcome
frameworks.lede: An outcome-based market only stays credible if these five are never blurred. Guarantees without validated causal measurement would collapse trust.
frameworks.sourceLabel: From Media Buying to Outcome Engineering

frameworks.name: Graduated autonomy
frameworks.lede: Remove manual work, keep accountability. Autonomy cannot scale without identity, permissions and audit, so it is granted one level at a time.

stages.name: Plan for review
stages.detail: A plan is drafted for review.

stages.name: Highly autonomous
stages.detail: The system acts with minimal oversight.

frameworks.sourceLabel: From Media Buying to Outcome Engineering
